data.narrative:
Arbor Energy is a Series A climate & energy company founded by Brad Hartwig that has raised $96M to date. The valuation universe comprises 9 same-sector peers: 1 public company (LNZA) and 8 private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable and yields a $192M valuation, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $96M capital raised proxy. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable given insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum thresholds (0 narrow-filter matches across the Climate & Energy sector peer set of 9 firms); reliance on all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise. No revenue or profitability data are available to support revenue multiple or DCF-based approaches.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $163M (low) to $221M (high), with a median of $192M. This range reflects stage-typical expansion multiples applied to observed capital. Key uncertainties stem from the single-method foundation of this conclusion: the absence of narrow peer multiples leaves the analysis vulnerable to stage-timing assumptions and limits cross-validation. Additional disclosure of financial metrics (revenue, burn rate, unit economics) and closer-stage peer transactions would materially improve precision.
